_comment: Regression corpus for examples/eval.rs: five short recordings of one speaker,
one microphone, with hand-verified ground truth ("reference") for each.
This is a regression proxy, not an accuracy benchmark -- see docs/evaluation.md.
'exercises' names the specific wording each clip is known to be sensitive to,
for a human reading a WER change; it is documentation, not something the eval
checks programmatically. 'long_clip_check' marks the one clip that must
additionally decode to non-empty text well inside its own duration.

samples.reference: So, this is a test. Let's try some commands here. Let's make a dir with the command mkdir named test and touch a new file test_file and then rm -rf this whole folder again.
exercises: commands -> comments: technical word lost to a common English neighbour
a dir -> there: context error, hotword biasing cannot fix this
mkdir -> MK D I R / mkir
rm -rf -> RMRF: command name run together
test_file -> test underscore file: spoken punctuation not symbolised
Very short utterance. Primary check that pre-roll keeps the first word:
at 1.3s there is no room to lose the leading 'cd' and still score.

samples.reference: I have udev rules, udev rules to set the keyboard layout, but I think something you did reset it.
exercises: set -> sed and reset -> rust: a fuzzy-replacement failure this project bans
(see docs/constraints.md#bias-vocabulary-at-decode-time-never-fuzzy-replacement).
MUST still decode 'set' and 'reset' correctly.

samples.reference: The replacements are too stringent, for example set S E T you corrected to sed S E D, which doesn't really make sense. Also reset R E S E T you fix to Rust R U S T. So I think it's too stringent. Also can you fix the overlay? What we have right now is okay. There's the window is too small. So maybe that needs some I3 rules, I'm not sure.
exercises: The longest clip: a one-shot decode must return non-empty text comfortably
inside its own duration -- see 'long_clip_check' below.
set/sed and reset/rust are each spoken TOGETHER, in the same sentence, plus
spelled out letter by letter. Any fuzzy replacement collapses one onto the
other and loses the meaning entirely; exact whole-word matching must not.
'i3' is a bare hotword candidate -- currently mis-rendered.

samples.reference: Okay, we are now at the new model. The overlay is there but not wide enough. And okay, let's see the text quality. But I think the whole system is not great, so maybe before we build our own we should uninstall and reset everything and then try a structured approach to write a plan and then build it.
exercises: Near-clean prose; only known error is 'system' -> 'systemd'.
Useful as an upper baseline -- if hotword biasing degrades this sample,
hotwords_score is too high.
Also over 25s, so it is a second guard against any decode time-out.
